\section{Introduction}

\subsection{Provability as a modality}

The provability predicate of a sufficiently strong arithmetical theory obeys the
Hilbert--Bernays--L\"ob derivability conditions, and the propositional modal principles
it validates are exactly the theorems of the G\"odel--L\"ob logic \textbf{GL},
axiomatized over classical propositional logic by
\[
\textbf{K.}\ \Box(a \to b) \to (\Box a \to \Box b), \qquad
\textbf{4.}\ \Box a \to \Box\Box a, \qquad
\textbf{L\"ob.}\ \Box(\Box a \to a) \to \Box a,
\]
together with modus ponens and necessitation. The second incompleteness theorem is the
instance $a := \bot$ of L\"ob's axiom.

A single box captures one notion of provability; practice is full of several: proofs in
a base theory, proofs in an extension, proofs of bounded length, proofs using restricted
induction. Each is a \emph{tag} $i$ carrying its own operator $\Box_i$, individually a GL
modality; the interesting phenomena arise from what the ambient theory proves about the
\emph{interaction} of tags.

\subsection{Two invariants}

Throughout, $S$ is a consistent theory with a distinguished set of theorems, written
$\vdash a$, all of whose tags are GL tags (Definition~\ref{def:gl}).

\paragraph{Inconsistency height.} The iterated boxed falsum $\Box_i^k\bot$ is monotone in
$k$. When the transition to provability happens at a finite point we write
$\vdash \Box_i^k \bot \iff H_i < k$ and call $H_i$ the \emph{inconsistency height} of tag
$i$. A tag of height $0$ is \emph{dead}; a tag of height $H$ supports a tower of $H$
nested consistency assertions.

\paragraph{Reflection depth.} Full reflection is unavailable, but reflection restricted
by modal complexity is not. Writing $\bd(a)$ for the box depth of $a$, say that tag $i$
\emph{reflects to depth $r$} if $\vdash \Box_i a$ implies $\vdash a$ for every $a$ with
$\bd(a) < r$. This is monotone downward in $r$, so there is a well-defined
\emph{reflection depth} $\rho_i = \sup\{ r : \text{tag } i \text{ reflects to depth } r\}$;
$\rho_i = 0$ holds trivially. Reflection depth is a resolution parameter: how modally
complex a statement must be before the theory's trust in $\Box_i$ becomes unwarranted.

\subsection{The realizability question and our results}

Since a formula of box depth $\ge H_i$ can already exhibit the collapse of the tag, one
expects $\rho_i \le H_i$, and it is natural to conjecture this is the only constraint,
the picture being that the height is the distance from the top of a finite chain to the
point where a tag's accessibility switches off, while the depth is the distance from the
top to the point where the valuation stops being constant --- two independent cut points.
We prove that this is not so. Our contributions are: a general semantic framework
(\S\ref{sec:frames}); the image theorem and its corollaries (\S\ref{sec:image}); rigidity
and the refutation (\S\ref{sec:rigidity}); the height-gap inequality and the low-tag
collapse (\S\ref{sec:gap}); exact spectra for constant and two-valued height vectors
(\S\ref{sec:spectra}); decoupling by window frames (\S\ref{sec:window}); and algorithms
with a numerical census (\S\ref{sec:algorithms}--\S\ref{sec:census}).

\section{The language and the invariants}

\begin{definition}[Formulas]
Fix countably many atoms $p_0,p_1,\dots$ and countably many tags $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
Formulas are generated by $a ::= \bot \mid p_n \mid (a \to a) \mid \Box_i a$. We
abbreviate $\neg a := a \to \bot$ and write $\Box_i^k a$ for the $k$-fold iterate, with
$\Box_i^0 a = a$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Box depth]
$\bd(\bot) = \bd(p_n) = 0$, $\bd(a \to b) = \max(\bd(a),\bd(b))$, and
$\bd(\Box_i a) = \bd(a)+1$. In particular $\bd(\Box_i^k a) = k + \bd(a)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[GL tag, consistency]\label{def:gl}
A \emph{theory} is a set $S$ of formulas, whose members we call theorems and write
$\vdash a$. The tag $i$ is a \emph{GL tag} of $S$ if $S$ is closed under modus ponens and
under necessitation for $\Box_i$, contains all propositional tautologies, and contains
all instances of \textbf{K}, \textbf{4} and \textbf{L\"ob} for $\Box_i$. $S$ is
\emph{consistent} if $\nvdash \bot$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Height and depth]
For a consistent theory all of whose tags are GL tags: the \emph{inconsistency height} of
tag $i$ is the number $H_i$ (if it exists) with $\vdash \Box_i^k\bot \iff H_i < k$; tag
$i$ \emph{reflects to depth $r$}, written $\Refl(r,i)$, if $\vdash \Box_i a$ implies
$\vdash a$ for every $a$ with $\bd(a) < r$; and
$\rho_i = \sup\{r : \Refl(r,i)\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the rule]
If $r' \le r$ and $\Refl(r,i)$, then $\Refl(r',i)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The hypothesis of the rule at $r'$ constrains a subset of the formulas constrained at
$r$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Realizability]\label{def:realize}
Fix a \emph{truncation level} $N$. Vectors $d,\rho : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ are
\emph{realized} by a theory $S$ if for all $i,k,r$,
\[
\vdash \Box_i^k\bot \iff \min(N,d_i) < k, \qquad \Refl(r,i) \iff r \le \rho_i .
\]
\end{definition}

The \emph{naive conjecture} is: for every $N$ and all $d,\rho$ with
$\rho_i \le \min(N,d_i)$, some theory of the truncated class
(Definition~\ref{def:trunc}) realizes $(d,\rho)$.

\section{Tag-indexed frames with a valuation}\label{sec:frames}

\begin{definition}[Frame, valuation, model]
A \emph{tag-indexed frame} is a family of relations $R_i$, written $R_i(m,n)$ and used
only for $n<m$. A \emph{valuation} assigns a truth value $V(m,p)$ to every world $m$ and
atom $p$. Satisfaction is defined by: $m \nvDash \bot$; $m \vDash p \iff V(m,p)$;
$m \vDash a \to b$ iff $m\vDash a$ implies $m \vDash b$; and $m \vDash \Box_i a$ iff
$n \vDash a$ for every $n<m$ with $R_i(m,n)$. The theory of the model truncated at $N$,
written $\Th_N(R,V)$, consists of the formulas true at every world $m \le N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Transitivity]
$R_i$ is \emph{transitive} if $R_i(m,n)$ and $R_i(n,k)$ imply $R_i(m,k)$ for all
$k<n<m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness]\label{thm:sound}
If $R_i$ is transitive then $i$ is a GL tag of $\Th_N(R,V)$, for every $N$ and $V$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Modus ponens, necessitation, tautologies and \textbf{K} are immediate from the truth
clauses; \textbf{4} is exactly transitivity. For \textbf{L\"ob}, fix $m \le N$ with
$m \vDash \Box_i(\Box_i a \to a)$ and show by strong induction on $n$ that every $n<m$
with $R_i(m,n)$ satisfies $a$: the induction hypothesis together with transitivity gives
$n \vDash \Box_i a$, and $n \vDash \Box_i a \to a$ then yields $n \vDash a$. Hence
$m \vDash \Box_i a$. Converse well-foundedness --- the usual side condition for L\"ob ---
is automatic, since the semantics only descends through the natural numbers.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Consistency]
$\Th_N(R,V)$ is consistent for all $R,V,N$: $\bot$ fails at the world $0$. \qed
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The image theorem}\label{sec:image}

\begin{definition}[Image]
The \emph{image} of tag $i$ in the truncation at $N$ is
$\Imag_i = \{ n : \exists m \le N,\ n<m \text{ and } R_i(m,n)\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Image theorem]\label{thm:image}
For every formula $a$,
$\Th_N(R,V) \vdash \Box_i a$ if and only if $n \vDash a$ for every $n \in \Imag_i$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) For $n \in \Imag_i$ pick $m \le N$ with $n<m$ and $R_i(m,n)$; since
$\Box_i a$ holds at $m$, $a$ holds at $n$. ($\Leftarrow$) Every $R_i$-successor of a
world $m \le N$ lies in $\Imag_i$, so $m \vDash \Box_i a$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reflection as indistinguishability]\label{cor:indist}
Tag $i$ reflects to depth $r$ iff no formula of box depth $<r$ is true throughout
$\Imag_i$ and false at some world $\le N$. \qed
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity in the image]\label{thm:mono}
If $\Imag_i \subseteq \Imag_j$ then $\Refl(r,i)$ implies $\Refl(r,j)$ for every $r$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $\bd(a)<r$ and $\vdash \Box_j a$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:image}, $a$ holds throughout
$\Imag_j \supseteq \Imag_i$, hence throughout $\Imag_i$, i.e.\ $\vdash \Box_i a$; apply
$\Refl(r,i)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Equal images, equal rules]\label{cor:equal}
If $\Imag_i = \Imag_j$ then $\Refl(r,i) \iff \Refl(r,j)$ for all $r$; in particular
$\rho_i = \rho_j$. \qed
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Decoupling requires incomparability]\label{cor:incomp}
If $\Refl(r,i)$ holds and $\Refl(r,j)$ fails then $\Imag_i \not\subseteq \Imag_j$. Hence
in any model whose tag images form a chain under inclusion, reflection depths are
monotone in the images, and equal images force equal depths. \qed
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Bounded bisimulation}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded bisimulation transfer]\label{thm:bisim}
Let $E_0,E_1,\dots$ be relations between worlds such that (i) each $E_k$ is symmetric;
(ii) $E_k$-related worlds agree on all atoms; and (iii) if $E_{k+1}(m,n)$ and $m'<m$ with
$R_j(m,m')$, then there is $n'<n$ with $R_j(n,n')$ and $E_k(m',n')$. Then $E_k(m,n)$
implies that $m$ and $n$ satisfy the same formulas of box depth $\le k$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction on the formula; atoms use (ii) and implication is componentwise. For
$\Box_j b$ with $\bd(\Box_j b) \le k+1$, suppose $m \vDash \Box_j b$ and let $n'<n$ with
$R_j(n,n')$. By (i) and (iii) applied at $n$ there is $m'<m$ with $R_j(m,m')$ and
$E_k(n',m')$; then $m' \vDash b$, so $n' \vDash b$ by the induction hypothesis since
$\bd(b) \le k$. The other direction is symmetric.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Depth zero]\label{lem:depth0}
If $V(m,\cdot) = V(n,\cdot)$ then $m$ and $n$ satisfy the same formulas of box depth $0$.
\qed
\end{lemma}

\section{Truncated frames and the rigidity theorem}\label{sec:rigidity}

\begin{definition}[Truncated frames]\label{def:trunc}
For a truncation vector $c$, let $R^c_i(m,n) \iff m \le c_i$: tag $i$ inspects everything
below $m$ as long as $m \le c_i$, and nothing at all from higher worlds. Write
$\mathrm{Trunc}_N(c,V) = \Th_N(R^c,V)$; these frames are transitive, so every such theory
is consistent with all tags GL tags. The \emph{truncated class at level $N$} is the family
of all $\mathrm{Trunc}_N(c,V)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Height spectrum]\label{lem:height}
In $\mathrm{Trunc}_N(c,V)$: $\vdash \Box_i^k\bot \iff \min(N,c_i)<k$; thus
$H_i = \min(N,c_i)$, independently of the valuation.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
One computes $m \vDash \Box_i^k\bot$ iff $k \ge 1$ and ($c_i<m$ or $m<k$): above the cut
the boxes are vacuous, below it each box strips one world off the chain. Evaluating at
$m=0$ and $m=\min(N,c_i)$ gives both directions.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Image of a truncated tag]\label{lem:capimage}
$\Imag_i = [\,0,\min(N,c_i)\,)$, an initial segment; hence $\vdash \Box_i a$ iff
$n \vDash a$ for all $n < \min(N,c_i)$. \qed
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity]\label{thm:rigid}
In $\mathrm{Trunc}_N(c,V)$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item if $\min(N,c_i) \le \min(N,c_j)$ then $\Refl(r,i)$ implies $\Refl(r,j)$ for all $r$;
in particular $\rho_i \le \rho_j$;
\item if $\min(N,c_i) = \min(N,c_j)$ then $\Refl(r,i) \iff \Refl(r,j)$ for all $r$,
whatever the valuation; in particular $\rho_i = \rho_j$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Initial segments are totally ordered by inclusion; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:mono} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:equal} through Lemma~\ref{lem:capimage}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Levelwise constancy]\label{thm:levelwise}
If a truncated model realizes $(d,\rho)$ at level $N$ and $\min(N,d_i) = \min(N,d_j)$,
then $\rho_i = \rho_j$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Realizing the height vector forces $\min(N,c_i) = \min(N,d_i)$ for every $i$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:height} at $k = \min(N,c_i)+1$ and $k = \min(N,d_i)+1$. The tags then have
equal truncated heights, so by Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}(2) each satisfies the other's
reflection rules; realizing the depth vector turns this into $\rho_i \le \rho_j$ and
$\rho_j \le \rho_i$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The refuting profile]\label{def:refute}
At level $N=2$ set $d_i = 2$ for $i \le 1$ and $d_i = 0$ for $i \ge 2$; and $\rho_0 = 1$,
$\rho_i = 0$ for $i \ge 1$. Then $\rho_i \le \min(2,d_i)$ for every $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Refutation I]\label{thm:refute1}
No truncated model at level $2$ realizes the profile of Definition~\ref{def:refute}: the
tags $0$ and $1$ have equal truncated height $2$ but are prescribed reflection depths
$1 \ne 0$, contradicting Theorem~\ref{thm:levelwise}. Consequently it is \emph{not} the
case that every pair $(d,\rho)$ with $\rho_i \le \min(N,d_i)$ is realized by a truncated
model. \qed
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
Rigidity holds for arbitrary valuations, so no choice of atoms repairs the conjecture
inside the truncated class. The conjectured picture fails not because the valuation is
powerless --- \S\ref{sec:spectra} shows it is very powerful --- but because it is
\emph{global}: it cannot distinguish two tags at all.
\end{remark}

\section{The height-gap inequality}\label{sec:gap}

\begin{definition}[Gap probe]
For tags $i,j$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$, put
$G^{s}_{i,j} = \Box_i^{\,s}(\Box_j\bot \to \Box_i\bot)$, a formula of box depth exactly
$s+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Truth table of the gap probe]\label{lem:probe}
In a truncated model with vector $c$: $m \vDash G^s_{i,j}$ if and only if $c_i<m$ or
$m \le c_j + s$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction on $s$. For $s=0$ one has $m \vDash \Box_j\bot$ iff $m=0$ or $c_j<m$, and
similarly for $i$; the implication holds exactly when $c_i<m$ or $m \le c_j$. For the
step, $m \vDash \Box_i G^s_{i,j}$ is vacuous when $c_i<m$ and otherwise demands
$G^s_{i,j}$ at every $n<m$, which by hypothesis means $m \le c_j+s+1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Height-gap inequality]\label{thm:gap}
In a truncated model at level $N$, if $\min(N,c_j) < \min(N,c_i)$ then tag $i$ does not
reflect to depth $\min(N,c_i)-\min(N,c_j)+1$; hence $\rho_i \le H_i - H_j$ whenever
$H_j < H_i$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Write $h_i = \min(N,c_i)$, $h_j = \min(N,c_j)$, $s = h_i-h_j-1$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:probe}, $G^s_{i,j}$ is true at every $n<h_i$ (as $n \le h_j+s$), so
$\vdash \Box_i G^s_{i,j}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:capimage}; its box depth is $h_i-h_j$. But
$G^s_{i,j}$ fails at the world $h_i \le N$, since $h_i \le c_i$ and $h_i > h_j+s$. So the
probe is provably necessary and not a theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Low-tag collapse]\label{thm:low}
In a truncated model, if $\min(N,c_j) < \min(N,c_i)$ then tag $j$ does not reflect to
depth $2$; hence $\rho_j \le 1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The probe at distance $0$ is the depth-one formula $\Box_j\bot \to \Box_i\bot$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:probe} it holds at every $n \le c_j$, in particular throughout
$\Imag_j = [0,h_j)$, and fails at the world $h_j+1 \le h_i \le N$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Deep tags share a height]
If a truncated model realizes $(d,\rho)$ and $\rho_i,\rho_j \ge 2$, then
$\min(N,d_i) = \min(N,d_j)$: non-trivial reflection occurs only on a single level set of
the height vector. \qed
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Refutation II]
At level $N=2$ let $d_0 = 2$, $d_i = 1$ for $i \ge 1$, and $\rho_i = d_i$ (each tag asked
for the maximum its own height permits). No truncated model realizes this profile:
Theorem~\ref{thm:gap} gives $\rho_0 \le 2-1 = 1 < 2$. Thus the conjecture fails for a
second, independent reason --- the \emph{joint} height vector constrains each single
reflection depth. \qed
\end{theorem}

\section{Exact spectra inside the truncated class}\label{sec:spectra}

\begin{definition}[Block valuation]
For $t \in \mathbb{N}$ let $V^t(m,p)$ be true exactly when $m<t$: the atoms mark an
initial block of the chain with \emph{cut point} $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform realizability]\label{thm:const}
For all $\rho \le N$, the truncated model with $c_i = N$ for every tag and valuation
$V^{\,N-\rho}$ realizes the constant profile $d \equiv N$, $\rho \equiv \rho$. Every tag
has reflection depth exactly the distance from the top of the chain to the cut point of
the valuation.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Heights are immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem:height}. Since every tag sees all worlds below
the current one, the model is the single-tag chain with a block valuation, whose spectrum
is $\{r : r \le N-t\}$ for cut point $t$: no formula of box depth $<N-t$ separates the top
world $N$ from $N-1 \in \Imag$, while a formula of box depth $N-t$ counts the distance
from the top down to the block.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Two-valued vectors]
Fix $1 \le L < N$ and a set of ``high'' tags. The two-valued truncation vector assigns
$c_i = N$ to a high tag and $c_i = L$ to a low tag; take the \emph{flat} valuation $V^0$,
in which no atom is ever true.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Horizon lemma]\label{thm:horizon}
Suppose every tag has $c_j = L$ or $c_j \ge N$. Then under the flat valuation, for all
$m,n \le N$ and all $k$, $\min(m,L+k) = \min(n,L+k)$ implies that $m$ and $n$ satisfy the
same formulas of box depth $\le k$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:bisim} with $E_k(m,n) :\iff m,n \le N$ and
$\min(m,L+k) = \min(n,L+k)$. Symmetry is clear and the atom clause is trivial. For the
back-and-forth condition at $E_{k+1}$, let $m'<m$ with $R^c_j(m,m')$. If $j$ is low then
$m \le L$ and the horizon condition forces $m=n$, so $m'$ matches itself; if $j$ is high,
match $m'$ with $\min(m',L+k)$, which is $<n$ and $E_k$-related to $m'$ by construction.
\end{proof}

Informally: the low tags freeze the visible horizon at $L$, and each box moves it down by
one, so a formula of box depth $k$ can count no further than $L+k$.

\begin{theorem}[High tags reflect to the gap]\label{thm:high}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:horizon} with $L<N$, every high tag reflects to
depth $N-L$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $\bd(a) \le N-L-1$ and let $a$ hold throughout $\Imag_i = [0,N)$. For $m<N$ this is
immediate; for $m=N$ apply Theorem~\ref{thm:horizon} with $k = N-L-1$ to $m=N$ and
$n=N-1$, since $\min(N,L+k) = \min(N-1,L+k) = N-1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Live tags reflect to depth one]\label{thm:one}
Under the flat valuation, if $\min(N,c_j) \ge 1$ then tag $j$ reflects to depth $1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A formula of box depth $0$ has the same truth value at all worlds
(Lemma~\ref{lem:depth0}); its truth at $0 \in \Imag_j$ propagates everywhere.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact two-valued spectrum]\label{thm:twoval}
Let $1 \le L < N$ and split the tags into a nonempty set of high tags (height $N$) and a
nonempty set of low tags (height $L$). The truncated model with the flat valuation
realizes exactly $\rho_{\mathrm{high}} = N-L$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{low}} = 1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Heights: Lemma~\ref{lem:height}. Upper bounds: Theorems~\ref{thm:gap} and \ref{thm:low}.
Lower bounds: Theorems~\ref{thm:high} and \ref{thm:one}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sharpness]
The height-gap inequality and the low-tag collapse are attained simultaneously; on height
vectors with at most two values the reflection-depth vector is a computable function of
the height vector. \qed
\end{corollary}

\section{Decoupling by window frames}\label{sec:window}

\begin{definition}[Window frames]
Given bottom cuts $b$ and top cuts $H$, let $R^{b,H}_i(m,n) \iff m \le H_i$ and
$n \ge b_i$: tag $i$ looks down only from the worlds $m \le H_i$ and only onto the worlds
$n \ge b_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
Window frames are transitive, hence yield consistent GL theories; moreover
$\vdash \Box_i^k\bot \iff \min(N,H_i)-b_i < k$ and
$\Imag_i = [\,b_i,\min(N,H_i)\,)$. The height is the length of the window and the image is
an \emph{interval} --- and intervals can be incomparable. \qed
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The decoupling model]\label{def:fam}
Fix $h \ge 2$ and take the chain $0,1,\dots,h+1$ (so $N = h+1$). Put $b_0 = 0$,
$H_0 = h$; $b_1 = 1$, $H_1 = h+1$; $H_i = 0$ for $i \ge 2$; and let the valuation be
$V^1$, so every atom is true exactly at the world $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equal heights]
Both live tags have inconsistency height $h$: $\min(h+1,h)-0 = h$ for tag $0$ and
$\min(h+1,h+1)-1 = h$ for tag $1$. Every tag $i \ge 2$ is dead. \qed
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tag $1$ reflects to depth $0$]
For $h \ge 1$, tag $1$ does not reflect to depth $1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\Imag_1 = [1,h+1)$ lies entirely above the block of the valuation, so the box-free
formula $\neg p_0$ is true throughout it and $\vdash \Box_1 \neg p_0$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:image}. But $\neg p_0$ fails at the world $0$, which lies in the model
and outside $\Imag_1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Tag $0$ reflects to depth exactly $1$]
For $h \ge 2$, tag $0$ reflects to depth $1$ but not to depth $2$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\emph{Depth $1$.} $\Imag_0 = [0,h)$ contains the world $0$, where $p_0$ holds, and the
world $1$, where it does not --- a representative of each atom pattern of the model. A
box-free formula true throughout $\Imag_0$ therefore holds at $0$ and at $1$, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:depth0} its value at any $m \ge 1$ equals its value at $1$; so it is a
theorem. \emph{Not depth $2$.} Consider $\Box_0\bot \to \Box_1\bot$, of box depth $1$.
Here $\Box_0\bot$ holds at $m$ iff $m=0$ or $m>h$, and $\Box_1\bot$ holds at $m$ iff
$m \le 1$ or $m>h+1$. The implication is true at every $n<h$, hence provably necessary at
tag $0$; but at the top world $h+1$ it fails, since tag $0$ is exhausted there while tag
$1$ still sees the worlds $1,\dots,h$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Decoupling]
For every $h \ge 2$ there is a consistent GL theory in which two tags have equal
inconsistency heights $h$ and reflection depths $1$ and $0$, all other tags being dead
with reflection depth $0$. In particular the profile of Definition~\ref{def:refute},
realized by no truncated model, is realized by a consistent GL theory (take $h=2$). \qed
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Incomparable images, as predicted]
In the decoupling model $\Imag_0 = [0,h)$ and $\Imag_1 = [1,h+1)$: the world $0$ lies in
the first only, the world $h$ in the second only. By Corollary~\ref{cor:incomp} this
incomparability is forced --- no model with nested tag images can separate the two depths.
\qed
\end{theorem}

\section{Algorithms}\label{sec:algorithms}

\paragraph{Inconsistency height.} Evaluate $\Box_i^k\bot$ at all worlds $\le N$ for
increasing $k$ and return the least $k$ giving a theorem, minus one. Since $H_i \le N$,
the cost is $O(N^3)$ on a chain of $N+1$ worlds; closed forms are available for the two
structured families.

\paragraph{Reflection depth by modal type refinement.} Enumerating formulas is
unnecessary. Define depth-$k$ modal types by refinement:
\[
\tau_0(m) = \bigl(V(m,p)\bigr)_p, \qquad
\tau_{k+1}(m) = \Bigl(\tau_0(m),\ \bigl(i,\ \{\tau_k(n) : n<m,\ R_i(m,n)\}\bigr)_i\Bigr).
\]
Two worlds share a depth-$k$ type iff they satisfy the same formulas of box depth $\le k$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:bisim} and the existence of characteristic formulas). By
Corollary~\ref{cor:indist},
\[
\Refl(r,i) \iff \text{every world } m \le N \text{ satisfies } \tau_{r-1}(m) = \tau_{r-1}(n)
\text{ for some } n \in \Imag_i,
\]
since a world whose type is unrealized in $\Imag_i$ is separated from $\Imag_i$ by the
negation of its characteristic formula, of box depth $r-1$. Refinement up to depth $k$
costs $O(k\,T\,N^2)$ for $T$ tags.

\paragraph{Profile census.} Enumerate frames from a parameterized family together with
valuations, compute $(\min(N,H_i))_i$ and $(\rho_i)_i$, and collect the profiles;
comparing with the profiles permitted by $\rho_i \le H_i$ yields the table below, each
missing entry being attributable to monotonicity, rigidity, the gap bound, or the low-tag
collapse.

\section{Numerical census}\label{sec:census}

Fix the truncation level $N=2$ and two live tags. The naive conjecture permits $36$
profiles $((H_0,H_1),(\rho_0,\rho_1))$ with $\rho_i \le H_i \le 2$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lc}
\toprule
model class & profiles realized (of 36) \\
\midrule
truncated frames, arbitrary valuation & 22 \\
window frames on up to five worlds, arbitrary valuation & 32 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Each of the $14$ profiles missed by the truncated class is accounted for: eight by
rigidity (the two with heights $(1,1)$ and unequal depths, and the six with heights
$(2,2)$ and unequal depths); four by the height-gap inequality, namely
$((1,2),(0,2))$, $((1,2),(1,2))$, $((2,1),(2,0))$ and $((2,1),(2,1))$; and two by
monotonicity of depth in height, namely $((1,2),(1,0))$ and $((2,1),(0,1))$. Of the $14$,
window frames on at most five worlds recover $10$: the six with heights $(2,2)$ and the
four blocked by the height gap.

The census also confirms the exact spectra: for the two-valued vector at level $N$ with
low value $L$ the measured depths are $N-L$ and $1$ for all $2 \le N \le 8$ and
$1 \le L < N$; for the constant vector with block cut $t$ the measured depth is $N-t$ for
all $1 \le N \le 7$ and $0 \le t \le N$.

\section{Discussion}

For a single self-referential system, L\"ob's theorem limits self-trust
\emph{predictably}: the reflection depth is exactly the distance from the top of the model
to the point where information stops varying (Theorem~\ref{thm:const}). Put several
systems in one universe and their trustworthiness becomes \emph{entangled}. If one tag is
strictly weaker than another, the theory can compare their collapse points with a very
cheap formula --- the gap probe, i.e.\ ``if the weak one is inconsistent, so am I'', boxed
a few times --- and that comparison caps the trust it can place in the strong tag
(Theorem~\ref{thm:gap}) while flattening its trust in the weak one
(Theorem~\ref{thm:low}). The escape route is equally informative: a theory can only be
blocked by comparisons it can \emph{make}, and tags whose fields of view are nested are
always comparable. Tags that differ in what they can see at the \emph{bottom} are
genuinely incomparable, and then their reflection depths become independent.

Two general lemmas carry the whole development: the image theorem, which converts every
statement about provable boxes into a statement about a set of worlds, and the
bounded-bisimulation principle, which converts every ``small formulas cannot see this''
claim into a back-and-forth game. Note also that transitivity of each tag's relation is
the \emph{only} hypothesis needed for GL here; converse well-foundedness is free because
a box inspects only strictly smaller worlds of a chain.

\paragraph{Limitations.} The theories considered are semantically presented and finitely
truncated: they are theories of finite models, capturing the modal shadow of provability
notions in the sense in which \textbf{GL} captures the modal shadow of a single
provability predicate. Arithmetical realization of a prescribed profile is not addressed,
and the positive results prescribe reflection depths exactly only for the structured
families considered.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{problem}[Full GL realizability of height--depth profiles]
For every $N$ and all $d,\rho$ with $\rho_i \le \min(N,d_i)$, is there a consistent GL
theory --- a finite transitive tag-indexed frame with a valuation, no longer required to
be truncated --- realizing both vectors exactly, in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:realize}? The reflection depth of a tag is the least $k$ at which its
image fails to realize every depth-$k$ modal type of the model, so realizing a whole
profile means engineering one finite type ladder in which the prescribed images sit at
prescribed rungs: a purely combinatorial packing problem about intervals and a valuation.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Classification by image posets]
Replace the height vector by the poset of tag images under inclusion together with the
type ladder of the model. Which posets arise, and which depth vectors are compatible with
a given poset? The truncated class is the case of a chain; window frames realize interval
orders.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Sharp thresholds for general height vectors]
For a height vector with $\ell$ distinct values, is the maximal depth of a tag always
determined by the nearest lower value (the local gap), or do further values interfere?
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Arithmetical realization]
Is there a multi-tag analogue of Solovay's theorem: given a profile realized by a finite
frame, are there arithmetical provability predicates whose modal behaviour matches it?
Bounded-length proof predicates and iterated consistency extensions are natural candidates.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Complexity of realizability]
Given a finite profile, decide whether some finite transitive tag-indexed frame realizes
it. Each candidate is checkable in polynomial time by \S\ref{sec:algorithms}, so the
question is the complexity of the search.
\end{problem}

\section{Conclusion}

Heights and reflection depths of provability tags are not independent coordinates. Where
each tag simply switches off above a level, the reflection depth is a monotone function of
the height, equal heights force equal depths, and a strictly lower tag caps a higher tag's
depth by the height gap and its own depth by $1$ --- all three obstructions witnessed by
one small family of formulas, and all three sharp, as the exact two-valued spectrum
$\rho_{\mathrm{high}} = N-L$, $\rho_{\mathrm{low}} = 1$ shows. One abstract fact explains
everything: a provable box sees only the image of its tag's accessibility relation, and
reflection depth is monotone in that image. Rigidity is nesting; freedom is
incomparability. Allowing a tag to be blind at the bottom as well as at the top restores
the freedom and yields, for every $h \ge 2$, consistent theories whose two tags have
identical towers of consistency statements and radically different claims on the theory's
trust.

Heights and reflection depths of tags in finite provability models
==================================================================

This script is a self-contained numerical companion to the article and paper
"Two Cut Points, One Chain: Heights and Reflection Depths of Provability Tags".

It implements, from scratch:

  *  the language of multi-tag modal formulas (bottom, atoms, implication and
     one box operator per tag),
  *  Kripke semantics on the finite chain of worlds 0, 1, ..., N in which each
     tag i carries its own accessibility relation R_i, restricted to strictly
     descending steps, together with a valuation V,
  *  the truncated theory of such a model (a formula is a theorem iff it is
     true at every world 0..N),
  *  the two numerical invariants of a tag:
         - the inconsistency height  H_i  (the least k with box_i^{k+1} bot a
           theorem, i.e. the length of the longest R_i-chain visible),
         - the reflection depth      rho_i (the largest r such that every
           formula of box depth < r that is provably necessary at i is itself
           a theorem),
  *  the two frame families of the paper: the *truncated* frames (tag i looks
     down from every world m <= c_i, and sees all of them) and the *window*
     frames (tag i looks down only from worlds m <= H_i and only onto worlds
     n >= b_i),
  *  the rigidity theorem, the height-gap inequality, the low-tag collapse,
     the exact two-valued spectrum, and the decoupling family that separates
     the reflection depths of two tags of equal height.

The reflection depth is computed exactly, without enumerating formulas, using
the depth-k modal type refinement described in the paper: a tag reflects to
depth r iff every world of the model is depth-(r-1) equivalent to some world
in the image of that tag's accessibility relation.

Run with:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Formulas
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Formula = Tuple  # ('bot',) | ('atom', p) | ('imp', a, b) | ('box', i, a)

BOT: Formula = ("bot",)


def atom(p: int) -> Formula:
    """The propositional atom number `p`."""
    return ("atom", p)


def imp(a: Formula, b: Formula) -> Formula:
    """Material implication `a -> b`."""
    return ("imp", a, b)


def box(i: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    """The box of tag `i` applied to `a`."""
    return ("box", i, a)


def neg(a: Formula) -> Formula:
    """Negation, encoded as `a -> bot`."""
    return imp(a, BOT)


def box_pow(i: int, k: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    """The `k`-fold iterated box of tag `i`."""
    out = a
    for _ in range(k):
        out = box(i, out)
    return out


def box_depth(a: Formula) -> int:
    """Maximal nesting depth of boxes."""
    head = a[0]
    if head in ("bot", "atom"):
        return 0
    if head == "imp":
        return max(box_depth(a[1]), box_depth(a[2]))
    return box_depth(a[2]) + 1


def show(a: Formula) -> str:
    """Human-readable rendering of a formula."""
    head = a[0]
    if head == "bot":
        return "⊥"
    if head == "atom":
        return f"p{a[1]}"
    if head == "imp":
        if a[2] == BOT:
            return f"¬{show(a[1])}"
        return f"({show(a[1])} → {show(a[2])})"
    return f"□{a[1]}{show(a[2])}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Models: a tag-indexed frame plus a valuation, truncated at N
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Frame = Callable[[int, int, int], bool]      # (tag, source world, target world)
Valuation = Callable[[int, int], bool]       # (world, atom)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Model:
    """A finite tag-indexed Kripke model on the worlds 0, ..., N."""

    R: Frame
    V: Valuation
    N: int
    tags: Tuple[int, ...]
    atoms: Tuple[int, ...] = (0,)

    def worlds(self) -> range:
        return range(self.N + 1)

    def sees(self, i: int, m: int, n: int) -> bool:
        """World `m` sees world `n` at tag `i` (only strictly downwards)."""
        return n < m and self.R(i, m, n)

    def successors(self, i: int, m: int) -> List[int]:
        return [n for n in range(m) if self.R(i, m, n)]

    # -- satisfaction ------------------------------------------------------

    def sat(self, m: int, a: Formula) -> bool:
        head = a[0]
        if head == "bot":
            return False
        if head == "atom":
            return self.V(m, a[1])
        if head == "imp":
            return (not self.sat(m, a[1])) or self.sat(m, a[2])
        i = a[1]
        return all(self.sat(n, a[2]) for n in self.successors(i, m))

    def provable(self, a: Formula) -> bool:
        """`a` is a theorem of the truncated theory: true at every world <= N."""
        return all(self.sat(m, a) for m in self.worlds())

    def consistent(self) -> bool:
        return not self.provable(BOT)

    # -- images ------------------------------------------------------------

    def image(self, i: int) -> FrozenSet[int]:
        """The set of worlds seen by *some* world of the model at tag `i`."""
        return frozenset(
            n for m in self.worlds() for n in range(m) if self.R(i, m, n)
        )

    # -- invariants --------------------------------------------------------

    def inconsistency_height(self, i: int, cap: int | None = None) -> int:
        """Least `H` with `box_i^{H+1} bot` a theorem (the tag's height)."""
        cap = self.N + 2 if cap is None else cap
        for k in range(cap + 2):
            if self.provable(box_pow(i, k + 1, BOT)):
                return k
        return cap + 1

    def depth_types(self, k: int) -> Dict[int, object]:
        """The depth-`k` modal type of every world, by partition refinement.

        Depth 0: the valuation pattern.  Depth k+1: the depth-0 pattern
        together with, for every tag, the set of depth-`k` types of the
        successors at that tag.
        """
        types: Dict[int, object] = {
            m: tuple(self.V(m, p) for p in self.atoms) for m in self.worlds()
        }
        for _ in range(k):
            nxt: Dict[int, object] = {}
            for m in self.worlds():
                succ = tuple(
                    (i, frozenset(types[n] for n in self.successors(i, m)))
                    for i in self.tags
                )
                nxt[m] = (types[m], succ)
            types = nxt
        return types

    def reflects_to_depth(self, i: int, r: int) -> bool:
        """Does every formula of box depth `< r` provably necessary at `i`
        follow?  Equivalently: is every world depth-(r-1) equivalent to some
        world in the image of tag `i`?"""
        if r == 0:
            return True
        types = self.depth_types(r - 1)
        img = self.image(i)
        realized = {types[n] for n in img}
        return all(types[m] in realized for m in self.worlds())

    def reflection_depth(self, i: int, cap: int = 12) -> int:
        """Largest `r <= cap` with `reflects_to_depth(i, r)`."""
        r = 0
        while r < cap and self.reflects_to_depth(i, r + 1):
            r += 1
        return r


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.  The two frame families
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def truncated_frame(c: Sequence[int]) -> Frame:
    """Tag `i` looks down from every world `m <= c_i`, and sees all of them.

    Its image is the initial segment [0, min(N, c_i)); such images are always
    nested, which is exactly the source of the rigidity phenomenon.
    """
    return lambda i, m, n: m <= c[i]


def window_frame(b: Sequence[int], H: Sequence[int]) -> Frame:
    """Tag `i` looks down from the worlds `m <= H_i`, onto the worlds `n >= b_i`.

    Its image is the interval [b_i, min(N, H_i)); such intervals can be
    incomparable, which is what makes decoupling possible.
    """
    return lambda i, m, n: m <= H[i] and n >= b[i]


def flat_valuation() -> Valuation:
    """No atom is ever true: worlds can only be separated by counting steps."""
    return lambda m, p: False


def block_valuation(t: int) -> Valuation:
    """Every atom is true exactly at the worlds strictly below `t`."""
    return lambda m, p: m < t

def demo_semantics() -> None:
    banner("1.  A first model: heights, images, reflection depths")
    N = 4
    c = [4, 2, 0]
    model = Model(truncated_frame(c), block_valuation(2), N, tags=(0, 1, 2))
    print(f"worlds 0..{N},  truncated frame with cuts c = {c},")
    print("valuation: the atom p0 is true exactly at the worlds 0 and 1.\n")
    print(f"{'tag':>4} {'image':>16} {'height':>8} {'reflection depth':>18}")
    for i in model.tags:
        img = sorted(model.image(i))

            f" {model.reflection_depth(i):>18}"
        )
    print("\nsample theorems:")
    for f in [box_pow(0, 5, BOT), box_pow(1, 3, BOT), box(2, BOT), atom(0)]:
        print(f"   {show(f):<12} provable? {model.provable(f)}")


def demo_rigidity() -> None:
    banner("2.  Rigidity: equal truncated heights force equal reflection depths")
    print("Exhaustive check over truncated frames on 0..N with three tags and")
    print("all block valuations: whenever min(N, c_i) = min(N, c_j) the two")
    print("reflection depths agree -- for every valuation.\n")
    violations = 0
    checked = 0
    for N in range(1, 5):
        for c in product(range(N + 2), repeat=3):
            for t in range(N + 2):
                model = Model(truncated_frame(list(c)), block_valuation(t), N,
                              tags=(0, 1, 2))
                depths = [model.reflection_depth(i) for i in model.tags]
                for i in range(3):
                    for j in range(3):
                        if min(N, c[i]) == min(N, c[j]):
                            checked += 1
                            if depths[i] != depths[j]:
                                violations += 1
    print(f"pairs of equal-height tags checked : {checked}")
    print(f"violations of rigidity found       : {violations}")
    assert violations == 0


def demo_gap_bound() -> None:
    banner("3.  The height-gap inequality and the low-tag collapse")
    print("If min(N, c_j) < min(N, c_i) then, in a truncated model,")
    print("     rho_i <= min(N, c_i) - min(N, c_j)     and     rho_j <= 1.")
    print("The witness for the first bound is the gap probe")
    print("     □_i^{gap-1} (□_j ⊥ → □_i ⊥),   of box depth exactly the gap.\n")
    bad = 0
    for N in range(1, 6):
        for c in product(range(N + 1), repeat=2):
            for t in range(N + 2):
                model = Model(truncated_frame(list(c)), block_valuation(t), N,
                              tags=(0, 1))
                rho = [model.reflection_depth(i) for i in model.tags]
                hi, hj = min(N, c[0]), min(N, c[1])
                if hj < hi and not (rho[0] <= hi - hj and rho[1] <= 1):
                    bad += 1
                if hi < hj and not (rho[1] <= hj - hi and rho[0] <= 1):
                    bad += 1
    print(f"counterexamples to either inequality: {bad}")
    assert bad == 0

    N, c = 5, [5, 2]
    model = Model(truncated_frame(c), flat_valuation(), N, tags=(0, 1))
    gap = min(N, c[0]) - min(N, c[1])
    probe = box_pow(0, gap - 1, imp(box(1, BOT), box(0, BOT)))
    print(f"\nexample N = {N}, c = {c}, gap = {gap}")
    print(f"   probe                     : {show(probe)}")
    print(f"   its box depth             : {box_depth(probe)}")
    print(f"   □_0(probe) provable?      : {model.provable(box(0, probe))}")
    print(f"   probe provable?           : {model.provable(probe)}")
    print(f"   measured rho_0            : {model.reflection_depth(0)}"
          f"   (predicted {gap})")
    print(f"   measured rho_1            : {model.reflection_depth(1)}"
          f"   (predicted 1)")


def demo_two_valued_spectrum() -> None:
    banner("4.  The exact spectrum of a two-valued height vector")
    print("Heights N (high tags) and L (low tags), 1 <= L < N, flat valuation.")
    print("Prediction: rho_high = N - L exactly, rho_low = 1 exactly.\n")
    print(f"{'N':>3} {'L':>3} {'rho_high':>10} {'N-L':>6} {'rho_low':>9}")
    ok = True
    for N in range(2, 9):
        for L in range(1, N):
            model = Model(truncated_frame([N, L]), flat_valuation(), N,
                          tags=(0, 1))
            rh = model.reflection_depth(0)
            rl = model.reflection_depth(1)
            ok &= (rh == N - L and rl == 1)
            if N <= 6:
                print(f"{N:>3} {L:>3} {rh:>10} {N - L:>6} {rl:>9}")
    print(f"\nall predictions matched for 2 <= N <= 8: {ok}")
    assert ok


def demo_constant_profile() -> None:
    banner("5.  The uniform profile is realizable: rho = distance to the block")
    print("All tags of height N, block valuation with cut point N - rho:")
    print("the reflection depth is exactly the distance from the top of the")
    print("chain to the point where the valuation changes.\n")
    print(f"{'N':>3} {'cut':>5} {'measured rho':>14} {'N - cut':>9}")
    ok = True
    for N in range(1, 8):
        for cut in range(0, N + 1):
            model = Model(truncated_frame([N, N]), block_valuation(cut), N,

            rho = model.reflection_depth(0)

            if N <= 5:
                print(f"{N:>3} {cut:>5} {rho:>14} {N - cut:>9}")
    print(f"\nall predictions matched for 1 <= N <= 7: {ok}")
    assert ok


def demo_decoupling_family() -> None:
    banner("6.  Decoupling: equal heights, different reflection depths")
    print("Window frame on the worlds 0..h+1:")
    print("   tag 0 looks down from the worlds m <= h and sees everything;")
    print("   tag 1 looks down from the worlds m <= h+1 but never sees world 0;")
    print("   the atom p0 is true exactly at the world 0.")
    print("Both tags have inconsistency height h, yet their reflection depths")
    print("are 1 and 0.  No truncated model can do this, by rigidity.\n")
    print(f"{'h':>3} {'H_0':>5} {'H_1':>5} {'rho_0':>7} {'rho_1':>7}"
          f" {'image of 0':>14} {'image of 1':>14}")
    for h in range(2, 7):
        b = [0, 1, 0]
        H = [h, h + 1, 0]
        model = Model(window_frame(b, H), block_valuation(1), h + 1,
                      tags=(0, 1, 2))
        print(
            f"{h:>3} {model.inconsistency_height(0):>5}"
            f" {model.inconsistency_height(1):>5}"
            f" {model.reflection_depth(0):>7} {model.reflection_depth(1):>7}"
            f" {str(sorted(model.image(0))):>14}"
            f" {str(sorted(model.image(1))):>14}"
        )
    h = 3
    model = Model(window_frame([0, 1, 0], [h, h + 1, 0]), block_valuation(1),
                  h + 1, tags=(0, 1, 2))
    im0, im1 = model.image(0), model.image(1)
    print(f"\nimages are incomparable at h = {h}: "
          f"{sorted(im0 - im1)} in image(0) only, "
          f"{sorted(im1 - im0)} in image(1) only.")
    print("separating formula for tag 1 (box depth 0):",
          show(neg(atom(0))),
          "-- necessary at tag 1, false at the root, hence not a theorem.")
    print("separating formula for tag 0 (box depth 1):",
          show(imp(box(0, BOT), box(1, BOT))),
          "-- necessary at tag 0, false at the top world.")


def demo_profile_census() -> None:
    banner("7.  Census of realizable profiles: truncated versus window frames")
    print("Two live tags and the truncation level N = 2.  A profile is a pair")
    print("((H_0, H_1), (rho_0, rho_1)) of truncated heights min(N, H_i) and")
    print("exact reflection depths.  We compare the profiles realized by")
    print("truncated models (any valuation) with those realized by window")
    print("models on up to five worlds, and with the profiles the naive")
    print("conjecture permits (rho_i <= H_i).\n")
    N = 2
    tags = (0, 1)

    def valuations(worlds: int) -> List[Valuation]:
        out: List[Valuation] = []
        for pattern in product([False, True], repeat=worlds + 1):
            out.append((lambda pat: (lambda m, p: pat[m]))(pattern))
        return out

    def profiles(frames, worlds: int
                 ) -> Set[Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]]:
        found = set()
        for R in frames:
            for V in valuations(worlds):
                model = Model(R, V, worlds, tags=tags)
                if not model.consistent():
                    continue
                heights = tuple(min(N, model.inconsistency_height(i))
                                for i in tags)
                depths = tuple(model.reflection_depth(i, cap=N + 2)
                               for i in tags)
                found.add((heights, depths))
        return found

    trunc_frames = [truncated_frame(list(c))
                    for c in product(range(N + 1), repeat=2)]
    conjectured = {
        ((h0, h1), (r0, r1))
        for h0 in range(N + 1) for h1 in range(N + 1)
        for r0 in range(h0 + 1) for r1 in range(h1 + 1)
    }
    trunc = profiles(trunc_frames, N)
    win: Set[Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]] = set()
    for worlds in range(N, N + 3):
        win |= profiles(
            [window_frame(list(b), list(H))
             for b in product(range(worlds + 2), repeat=2)
             for H in product(range(worlds + 2), repeat=2)],
            worlds,
        )
    print(f"profiles permitted by the naive conjecture : {len(conjectured)}")
    print(f"profiles realized by truncated models      : "
          f"{len(trunc & conjectured)}")
    print(f"profiles realized by window models         : "
          f"{len(win & conjectured)}")
    missing = sorted(conjectured - trunc)
    print(f"\nprofiles the truncated class misses ({len(missing)}):")
    for heights, depths in missing:
        reason: List[str] = []
        for i, j in ((0, 1), (1, 0)):
            if heights[i] < heights[j] and depths[i] > depths[j]:
                reason.append("monotonicity")
            if heights[j] < heights[i] and depths[i] > heights[i] - heights[j]:
                reason.append("gap bound")
            if heights[j] < heights[i] and depths[j] > 1:
                reason.append("low-tag collapse")
        if heights[0] == heights[1] and depths[0] != depths[1]:
            reason.append("rigidity")
        marker = "yes" if (heights, depths) in win else " no"
        print(f"   heights {heights}, depths {depths}"
              f"   blocked by: {', '.join(sorted(set(reason))):<40}"
              f" window model? {marker}")
    recovered = sorted((conjectured - trunc) & win)
    print(f"\nprofiles beyond the truncated class that window frames "
          f"do realize ({len(recovered)}):")
    for heights, depths in recovered:
        print(f"   heights {heights}, depths {depths}")


def main() -> None:
    demo_semantics()
    demo_rigidity()
    demo_gap_bound()
    demo_two_valued_spectrum()
    demo_constant_profile()
    demo_decoupling_family()
    demo_profile_census()
    print("\nAll demonstrations completed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Formulas
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Formula = Tuple  # ('bot',) | ('atom', p) | ('imp', a, b) | ('box', i, a)

BOT: Formula = ("bot",)


def atom(p: int) -> Formula:
    """The propositional atom number `p`."""
    return ("atom", p)


def imp(a: Formula, b: Formula) -> Formula:
    """Material implication `a -> b`."""
    return ("imp", a, b)


def box(i: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    """The box of tag `i` applied to `a`."""
    return ("box", i, a)


def neg(a: Formula) -> Formula:
    """Negation, encoded as `a -> bot`."""
    return imp(a, BOT)


def box_pow(i: int, k: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    """The `k`-fold iterated box of tag `i`."""
    out = a
    for _ in range(k):
        out = box(i, out)
    return out


def box_depth(a: Formula) -> int:
    """Maximal nesting depth of boxes."""
    head = a[0]
    if head in ("bot", "atom"):
        return 0
    if head == "imp":
        return max(box_depth(a[1]), box_depth(a[2]))
    return box_depth(a[2]) + 1


def show(a: Formula) -> str:
    """Human-readable rendering of a formula."""
    head = a[0]
    if head == "bot":
        return "⊥"
    if head == "atom":
        return f"p{a[1]}"
    if head == "imp":
        if a[2] == BOT:
            return f"¬{show(a[1])}"
        return f"({show(a[1])} → {show(a[2])})"
    return f"□{a[1]}{show(a[2])}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Models: a tag-indexed frame plus a valuation, truncated at N
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Frame = Callable[[int, int, int], bool]      # (tag, source world, target world)
Valuation = Callable[[int, int], bool]       # (world, atom)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Model:
    """A finite tag-indexed Kripke model on the worlds 0, ..., N."""

    R: Frame
    V: Valuation
    N: int
    tags: Tuple[int, ...]
    atoms: Tuple[int, ...] = (0,)

    def worlds(self) -> range:
        return range(self.N + 1)

    def sees(self, i: int, m: int, n: int) -> bool:
        """World `m` sees world `n` at tag `i` (only strictly downwards)."""
        return n < m and self.R(i, m, n)

    def successors(self, i: int, m: int) -> List[int]:
        return [n for n in range(m) if self.R(i, m, n)]

    # -- satisfaction ------------------------------------------------------

    def sat(self, m: int, a: Formula) -> bool:
        head = a[0]
        if head == "bot":
            return False
        if head == "atom":
            return self.V(m, a[1])
        if head == "imp":
            return (not self.sat(m, a[1])) or self.sat(m, a[2])
        i = a[1]
        return all(self.sat(n, a[2]) for n in self.successors(i, m))

    def provable(self, a: Formula) -> bool:
        """`a` is a theorem of the truncated theory: true at every world <= N."""
        return all(self.sat(m, a) for m in self.worlds())

    def consistent(self) -> bool:
        return not self.provable(BOT)

    # -- images ------------------------------------------------------------

    def image(self, i: int) -> FrozenSet[int]:
        """The set of worlds seen by *some* world of the model at tag `i`."""
        return frozenset(
            n for m in self.worlds() for n in range(m) if self.R(i, m, n)
        )

    # -- invariants --------------------------------------------------------

    def inconsistency_height(self, i: int, cap: int | None = None) -> int:
        """Least `H` with `box_i^{H+1} bot` a theorem (the tag's height)."""
        cap = self.N + 2 if cap is None else cap
        for k in range(cap + 2):
            if self.provable(box_pow(i, k + 1, BOT)):
                return k
        return cap + 1

    def depth_types(self, k: int) -> Dict[int, object]:
        """The depth-`k` modal type of every world, by partition refinement.

        Depth 0: the valuation pattern.  Depth k+1: the depth-0 pattern
        together with, for every tag, the set of depth-`k` types of the
        successors at that tag.
        """
        types: Dict[int, object] = {
            m: tuple(self.V(m, p) for p in self.atoms) for m in self.worlds()
        }
        for _ in range(k):
            nxt: Dict[int, object] = {}
            for m in self.worlds():
                succ = tuple(
                    (i, frozenset(types[n] for n in self.successors(i, m)))
                    for i in self.tags
                )
                nxt[m] = (types[m], succ)
            types = nxt
        return types

    def reflects_to_depth(self, i: int, r: int) -> bool:
        """Does every formula of box depth `< r` provably necessary at `i`
        follow?  Equivalently: is every world depth-(r-1) equivalent to some
        world in the image of tag `i`?"""
        if r == 0:
            return True
        types = self.depth_types(r - 1)
        img = self.image(i)
        realized = {types[n] for n in img}
        return all(types[m] in realized for m in self.worlds())

    def reflection_depth(self, i: int, cap: int = 12) -> int:
        """Largest `r <= cap` with `reflects_to_depth(i, r)`."""
        r = 0
        while r < cap and self.reflects_to_depth(i, r + 1):
            r += 1
        return r


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.  The two frame families
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def truncated_frame(c: Sequence[int]) -> Frame:
    """Tag `i` looks down from every world `m <= c_i`, and sees all of them.

    Its image is the initial segment [0, min(N, c_i)); such images are always
    nested, which is exactly the source of the rigidity phenomenon.
    """
    return lambda i, m, n: m <= c[i]


def window_frame(b: Sequence[int], H: Sequence[int]) -> Frame:
    """Tag `i` looks down from the worlds `m <= H_i`, onto the worlds `n >= b_i`.

    Its image is the interval [b_i, min(N, H_i)); such intervals can be
    incomparable, which is what makes decoupling possible.
    """
    return lambda i, m, n: m <= H[i] and n >= b[i]


def flat_valuation() -> Valuation:
    """No atom is ever true: worlds can only be separated by counting steps."""
    return lambda m, p: False


def block_valuation(t: int) -> Valuation:
    """Every atom is true exactly at the worlds strictly below `t`."""
    return lambda m, p: m < t

def demo_profile_census() -> None:
    banner("7.  Census of realizable profiles: truncated versus window frames")
    print("Two live tags and the truncation level N = 2.  A profile is a pair")
    print("((H_0, H_1), (rho_0, rho_1)) of truncated heights min(N, H_i) and")
    print("exact reflection depths.  We compare the profiles realized by")
    print("truncated models (any valuation) with those realized by window")
    print("models on up to five worlds, and with the profiles the naive")
    print("conjecture permits (rho_i <= H_i).\n")
    N = 2
    tags = (0, 1)

    def valuations(worlds: int) -> List[Valuation]:
        out: List[Valuation] = []
        for pattern in product([False, True], repeat=worlds + 1):
            out.append((lambda pat: (lambda m, p: pat[m]))(pattern))
        return out

    def profiles(frames, worlds: int
                 ) -> Set[Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]]:
        found = set()
        for R in frames:
            for V in valuations(worlds):
                model = Model(R, V, worlds, tags=tags)
                if not model.consistent():
                    continue
                heights = tuple(min(N, model.inconsistency_height(i))
                                for i in tags)
                depths = tuple(model.reflection_depth(i, cap=N + 2)
                               for i in tags)
                found.add((heights, depths))
        return found

    trunc_frames = [truncated_frame(list(c))
                    for c in product(range(N + 1), repeat=2)]
    conjectured = {
        ((h0, h1), (r0, r1))
        for h0 in range(N + 1) for h1 in range(N + 1)
        for r0 in range(h0 + 1) for r1 in range(h1 + 1)
    }
    trunc = profiles(trunc_frames, N)
    win: Set[Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]] = set()
    for worlds in range(N, N + 3):
        win |= profiles(
            [window_frame(list(b), list(H))
             for b in product(range(worlds + 2), repeat=2)
             for H in product(range(worlds + 2), repeat=2)],
            worlds,
        )
    print(f"profiles permitted by the naive conjecture : {len(conjectured)}")
    print(f"profiles realized by truncated models      : "
          f"{len(trunc & conjectured)}")
    print(f"profiles realized by window models         : "
          f"{len(win & conjectured)}")
    missing = sorted(conjectured - trunc)
    print(f"\nprofiles the truncated class misses ({len(missing)}):")
    for heights, depths in missing:
        reason: List[str] = []
        for i, j in ((0, 1), (1, 0)):
            if heights[i] < heights[j] and depths[i] > depths[j]:
                reason.append("monotonicity")
            if heights[j] < heights[i] and depths[i] > heights[i] - heights[j]:
                reason.append("gap bound")
            if heights[j] < heights[i] and depths[j] > 1:
                reason.append("low-tag collapse")
        if heights[0] == heights[1] and depths[0] != depths[1]:
            reason.append("rigidity")
        marker = "yes" if (heights, depths) in win else " no"
        print(f"   heights {heights}, depths {depths}"
              f"   blocked by: {', '.join(sorted(set(reason))):<40}"
              f" window model? {marker}")
    recovered = sorted((conjectured - trunc) & win)
    print(f"\nprofiles beyond the truncated class that window frames "
          f"do realize ({len(recovered)}):")
    for heights, depths in recovered:
        print(f"   heights {heights}, depths {depths}")


def main() -> None:
    demo_semantics()
    demo_rigidity()
    demo_gap_bound()
    demo_two_valued_spectrum()
    demo_constant_profile()
    demo_decoupling_family()
    demo_profile_census()
    print("\nAll demonstrations completed.")

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Tuple

Frame = Callable[[int, int, int], bool]     # (tag, source world, target world)
Valuation = Callable[[int, int], bool]      # (world, atom)


def successors(R: Frame, i: int, m: int) -> List[int]:
    """The worlds that `m` inspects at tag `i` (always strictly below `m`)."""
    return [n for n in range(m) if R(i, m, n)]


def accessibility_image(R: Frame, N: int, i: int) -> FrozenSet[int]:
    """Im_i = { n : some world m <= N inspects n at tag i }."""
    return frozenset(n for m in range(N + 1) for n in successors(R, i, m))


def depth_types(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, tags: Sequence[int],
                atoms: Sequence[int], k: int) -> Dict[int, object]:
    """Depth-`k` modal types of all worlds 0..N, by partition refinement.

    tau_0(m)     = the atom pattern at m
    tau_{k+1}(m) = ( tau_0(m), ( i, { tau_k(n) : n inspected by m at i } )_i )

    Two worlds carry the same depth-k type iff they satisfy exactly the same
    formulas of box depth <= k.
    """
    types: Dict[int, object] = {
        m: tuple(V(m, p) for p in atoms) for m in range(N + 1)
    }
    for _ in range(k):
        refined: Dict[int, object] = {}
        for m in range(N + 1):
            profile: Tuple = tuple(
                (i, frozenset(types[n] for n in successors(R, i, m)))
                for i in tags
            )
            refined[m] = (types[m], profile)
        types = refined
    return types


def reflects_to_depth(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, tags: Sequence[int],
                      atoms: Sequence[int], i: int, r: int) -> bool:
    """Does every formula of box depth < r that is provably necessary at tag
    `i` follow?  Equivalently: is every world depth-(r-1) equivalent to some
    world in the image of tag `i`?"""
    if r == 0:
        return True
    types = depth_types(R, V, N, tags, atoms, r - 1)
    realized = {types[n] for n in accessibility_image(R, N, i)}
    return all(types[m] in realized for m in range(N + 1))


def reflection_depth(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, tags: Sequence[int],
                     atoms: Sequence[int] = (0,), i: int = 0,
                     cap: int = 16) -> int:
    """The reflection depth of tag `i`: the largest r <= cap for which the
    depth-restricted reflection rule is valid."""
    r = 0
    while r < cap and reflects_to_depth(R, V, N, tags, atoms, i, r + 1):
        r += 1
    return r

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, List, Tuple

Formula = Tuple
Frame = Callable[[int, int, int], bool]
Valuation = Callable[[int, int], bool]

BOT: Formula = ("bot",)


def imp(a: Formula, b: Formula) -> Formula:
    return ("imp", a, b)


def box(i: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    return ("box", i, a)


def box_pow(i: int, k: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    out = a
    for _ in range(k):
        out = box(i, out)
    return out


def box_depth(a: Formula) -> int:
    if a[0] in ("bot", "atom"):
        return 0
    if a[0] == "imp":
        return max(box_depth(a[1]), box_depth(a[2]))
    return box_depth(a[2]) + 1


def sat(R: Frame, V: Valuation, m: int, a: Formula) -> bool:
    """Truth of `a` at the world `m`; boxes look strictly downwards."""
    if a[0] == "bot":
        return False
    if a[0] == "atom":
        return V(m, a[1])
    if a[0] == "imp":
        return (not sat(R, V, m, a[1])) or sat(R, V, m, a[2])
    i = a[1]
    return all(sat(R, V, n, a[2]) for n in range(m) if R(i, m, n))


def provable(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, a: Formula) -> bool:
    """A theorem of the model truncated at N: true at every world 0..N."""
    return all(sat(R, V, m, a) for m in range(N + 1))


def inconsistency_height(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, i: int) -> int:
    """The least H with box_i^{H+1} bot a theorem."""
    for k in range(N + 2):
        if provable(R, V, N, box_pow(i, k + 1, BOT)):
            return k
    return N + 1


def gap_probe(i: int, j: int, s: int) -> Formula:
    """G^s_{i,j} = box_i^s ( box_j bot -> box_i bot ), of box depth s + 1."""
    return box_pow(i, s, imp(box(j, BOT), box(i, BOT)))


def probe_profile(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, i: int, j: int,
                  s: int) -> List[bool]:
    """Truth of the gap probe at each world 0..N."""
    probe = gap_probe(i, j, s)
    return [sat(R, V, m, probe) for m in range(N + 1)]


def gap_bound_witness(N: int, c: List[int], i: int, j: int
                      ) -> Tuple[Formula, int, bool, bool]:
    """In the truncated model with cuts `c`, return the probe that caps the
    reflection depth of the higher tag `i` against the lower tag `j`, its box
    depth, whether it is provably necessary at `i`, and whether it is a
    theorem."""
    R: Frame = lambda t, m, n: m <= c[t]
    V: Valuation = lambda m, p: False
    hi, hj = min(N, c[i]), min(N, c[j])
    probe = gap_probe(i, j, max(hi - hj - 1, 0))
    return (probe,
            box_depth(probe),
            provable(R, V, N, box(i, probe)),
            provable(R, V, N, probe))

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Frame = Callable[[int, int, int], bool]
Valuation = Callable[[int, int], bool]
Profile = Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]


# --- inlined primitives -----------------------------------------------------


def successors(R: Frame, i: int, m: int) -> List[int]:
    return [n for n in range(m) if R(i, m, n)]


def accessibility_image(R: Frame, N: int, i: int) -> Set[int]:
    return {n for m in range(N + 1) for n in successors(R, i, m)}


def inconsistency_height(R: Frame, N: int, i: int) -> int:
    """Least H with box_i^{H+1} bot true at every world: the longest R_i-chain
    starting at any world <= N."""
    chain: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for m in range(N + 1):
        chain[m] = max((chain[n] + 1 for n in successors(R, i, m)), default=0)
    return max(chain.values(), default=0)


def depth_types(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, tags: Sequence[int],
                k: int) -> Dict[int, object]:
    types: Dict[int, object] = {m: (V(m, 0),) for m in range(N + 1)}
    for _ in range(k):
        types = {
            m: (types[m], tuple((i, frozenset(types[n]
                                              for n in successors(R, i, m)))
                                for i in tags))
            for m in range(N + 1)
        }
    return types


def reflection_depth(R: Frame, V: Valuation, N: int, tags: Sequence[int],
                     i: int, cap: int) -> int:
    image = accessibility_image(R, N, i)
    r = 0
    while r < cap:
        types = depth_types(R, V, N, tags, r)
        realized = {types[n] for n in image}
        if not all(types[m] in realized for m in range(N + 1)):
            break
        r += 1
    return r


def truncated_frame(c: Sequence[int]) -> Frame:
    """Tag i inspects everything below m while m <= c_i (image = [0, min(N,c_i)))."""
    return lambda i, m, n: m <= c[i]


def window_frame(b: Sequence[int], H: Sequence[int]) -> Frame:
    """Tag i inspects n >= b_i from the worlds m <= H_i (image = [b_i, min(N,H_i)))."""
    return lambda i, m, n: m <= H[i] and n >= b[i]


def all_valuations(worlds: int) -> List[Valuation]:
    """Every 0/1 pattern of the single atom over the worlds 0..worlds."""
    out: List[Valuation] = []
    for pattern in product([False, True], repeat=worlds + 1):
        out.append((lambda pat: (lambda m, p: pat[m]))(pattern))
    return out


def profile_of(R: Frame, V: Valuation, worlds: int, N: int,
               tags: Sequence[int]) -> Profile:
    heights = tuple(min(N, inconsistency_height(R, worlds, i)) for i in tags)
    depths = tuple(reflection_depth(R, V, worlds, tags, i, cap=N + 2)
                   for i in tags)
    return heights, depths


def truncated_profiles(N: int, tags: Sequence[int] = (0, 1)) -> Set[Profile]:
    found: Set[Profile] = set()
    for c in product(range(N + 1), repeat=len(tags)):
        R = truncated_frame(list(c))
        for V in all_valuations(N):
            found.add(profile_of(R, V, N, N, tags))
    return found


def window_profiles(N: int, max_worlds: int,
                    tags: Sequence[int] = (0, 1)) -> Set[Profile]:
    found: Set[Profile] = set()
    for worlds in range(N, max_worlds + 1):
        for b in product(range(worlds + 2), repeat=len(tags)):
            for H in product(range(worlds + 2), repeat=len(tags)):
                R = window_frame(list(b), list(H))
                for V in all_valuations(worlds):
                    found.add(profile_of(R, V, worlds, N, tags))
    return found


def admissible_profiles(N: int) -> Set[Profile]:
    """Profiles the naive conjecture permits: rho_i <= H_i <= N."""
    return {
        ((h0, h1), (r0, r1))
        for h0 in range(N + 1) for h1 in range(N + 1)
        for r0 in range(h0 + 1) for r1 in range(h1 + 1)
    }


def obstructions(profile: Profile) -> List[str]:
    """Which proved obstruction rules out this profile inside the truncated
    class: monotonicity of depth in height, rigidity at equal heights, the
    height-gap inequality, or the low-tag collapse."""
    (h0, h1), (r0, r1) = profile
    heights, depths = (h0, h1), (r0, r1)
    reasons: List[str] = []
    for i, j in ((0, 1), (1, 0)):
        if heights[i] < heights[j] and depths[i] > depths[j]:
            reasons.append("monotonicity")
        if heights[j] < heights[i] and depths[i] > heights[i] - heights[j]:
            reasons.append("height-gap inequality")
        if heights[j] < heights[i] and depths[j] > 1:
            reasons.append("low-tag collapse")
    if heights[0] == heights[1] and depths[0] != depths[1]:
        reasons.append("rigidity")
    return sorted(set(reasons))


def census(N: int = 2, max_worlds: int = 4) -> Dict[str, object]:
    admissible = admissible_profiles(N)
    trunc = truncated_profiles(N) & admissible
    win = window_profiles(N, max_worlds) & admissible
    missing = sorted(admissible - trunc)
    return {
        "admissible": len(admissible),
        "truncated": len(trunc),
        "window": len(win),
        "missing": [(p, obstructions(p), p in win) for p in missing],
    }

    return {n for m in range(N + 1) for n in successors(R, i, m)}

from typing import Callable, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

Formula = Tuple
Frame = Callable[[int, int, int], bool]
Valuation = Callable[[int, int], bool]

BOT: Formula = ("bot",)


def imp(a: Formula, b: Formula) -> Formula:
    return ("imp", a, b)


def box(i: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    return ("box", i, a)


def box_pow(i: int, k: int, a: Formula) -> Formula:
    out = a
    for _ in range(k):
        out = box(i, out)
    return out


def sat(R: Frame, V: Valuation, m: int, a: Formula) -> bool:
    if a[0] == "bot":
        return False
    if a[0] == "atom":
        return V(m, a[1])
    if a[0] == "imp":
        return (not sat(R, V, m, a[1])) or sat(R, V, m, a[2])
    i = a[1]
    return all(sat(R, V, n, a[2]) for n in range(m) if R(i, m, n))

### A guided tour of heights, reflection depths, and why they are entangled

---

## 1. The question in one paragraph

Imagine a formal theory that can talk about several notions of provability at once — one for
a base system, one for an extension, one for proofs of bounded length. Write $\Box_i a$ for
"$a$ is provable at tag $i$". Each such operator obeys the laws of provability logic, in
particular **Löb's rule** $\Box(\Box a \to a) \to \Box a$, whose instance $a := \bot$ is
Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. Two numbers measure a tag:

* its **inconsistency height** $H_i$, defined by $\vdash \Box_i^k\bot \iff H_i < k$ — how tall
  a tower of nested consistency statements the tag supports;
* its **reflection depth** $\rho_i$ — the largest $r$ such that the theory can pass from
  "$a$ is provable at tag $i$" to "$a$" for every formula $a$ with fewer than $r$ nested boxes.

How much can these two numbers be chosen independently? That is the whole story below.

<details>
<summary><b>Background: box depth, and why full reflection is impossible</b></summary>

The **box depth** of a formula counts the maximal nesting of modal operators:
$\mathrm{bd}(\bot) = \mathrm{bd}(p) = 0$, $\mathrm{bd}(a \to b) = \max(\mathrm{bd}(a),\mathrm{bd}(b))$
and $\mathrm{bd}(\Box_i a) = \mathrm{bd}(a) + 1$. So $p \to q$ has depth $0$, $\Box_0 p$ has
depth $1$, and $\Box_0(\Box_1 p \to \Box_0\bot)$ has depth $2$.

A theory that could always infer $a$ from $\vdash \Box_i a$ would in particular infer $\bot$
from $\vdash \Box_i\bot$ — and, more subtly, Löb's rule already blocks full reflection even
for consistent tags. What survives is *reflection restricted by modal complexity*: a theory
may be perfectly willing to trust its tag on simple statements and not on complicated ones.
The reflection depth measures exactly where that willingness stops. Good background reading:
[provability logic](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-provability/) and
[Löb's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%B6b%27s_theorem).
</details>

---

## 2. Play with the models first

Everything below is about finite pictures: a chain of worlds $0, 1, \dots, N$, each tag looking
strictly *downwards* through its own accessibility relation, plus a valuation marking an initial
block of worlds. The theory of a picture is the set of formulas true at every world. Transitivity
of each relation is all that is needed for every tag to obey the laws of provability logic — the
usual well-foundedness requirement is automatic, since boxes only ever look down a finite chain.

Start by moving the sliders. Two things to try immediately: in **Truncated** mode, try to give the
two tags equal heights and different reflection depths (you will fail — that is the theorem); then
press **Decoupling model** and watch it happen in **Window** mode.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

<details>
<summary><b>How the reflection depth is computed exactly, without enumerating formulas</b></summary>

Give every world a **depth-$k$ modal type** by refinement: $\tau_0(m)$ is the atom pattern at $m$,
and $\tau_{k+1}(m)$ records $\tau_0(m)$ together with, for each tag, the set of depth-$k$ types of
the worlds $m$ can inspect. Two worlds share a depth-$k$ type exactly when they satisfy the same
formulas of box depth $\le k$ — a finite-resolution version of the classical
[bisimulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisimulation) idea.

Now the key reformulation. A provable box $\Box_i a$ says exactly that $a$ holds throughout the
**image** $\mathrm{Im}_i$ of the tag's accessibility relation — the set of worlds inspected by
somebody — while $\vdash a$ says $a$ holds at *every* world. So the tag reflects to depth $r$ iff
every world of the model is depth-$(r-1)$ equivalent to some world of $\mathrm{Im}_i$. That is a
finite check, and it is what the widget runs on every slider move.
</details>

---

## 3. The image theorem, and the one principle behind everything

> **Image theorem.** $\vdash \Box_i a$ if and only if $a$ is true at every world of
> $\mathrm{Im}_i = \{n : \text{some world } m \le N \text{ inspects } n \text{ at tag } i\}$.

Consequently, reflection depth is **monotone in the field of view**: if
$\mathrm{Im}_i \subseteq \mathrm{Im}_j$ then every reflection rule valid for $i$ is valid for $j$,
because the hypothesis "$a$ holds throughout the larger set" is the stronger one. Two tags with the
same field of view therefore obey *literally identical* reflection rules — and contrapositively:

> **To give two tags different reflection depths you must give them incomparable fields of view.**

The picture below is that sentence, drawn. On the left, a *truncated* model, where a tag simply
switches off above a level: its field of view is an initial segment, and initial segments are always
nested. On the right, a *window* model, where a tag may also be blind at the bottom: the fields of
view are intervals, and intervals can be incomparable.

{{visualization:0}}

## 4. Rigidity: the conjecture that had to fail

In a truncated model with cuts $c_i$, the height is $H_i = \min(N, c_i)$ — the valuation contributes
nothing — and the field of view is exactly $[0, H_i)$. Nested fields of view plus monotonicity give:

> **Rigidity.** In any truncated model, tags with equal heights have equal reflection depths, for
> *every* valuation; and the reflection depth is monotone in the height.

This kills the natural conjecture that heights and depths are freely choosable subject to
$\rho_i \le H_i$: ask for two tags of height $2$ with depths $1$ and $0$ and no truncated model with
any valuation obliges.

<details>
<summary><b>Why the conjecture was plausible in the first place — and the case where it is true</b></summary>

If all tags see everything below them and the atoms are true exactly at the worlds below a cut point
$t$, then every tag has reflection depth exactly $N - t$: the distance from the top of the chain to
the place where the valuation changes. So on constant height vectors the conjectural picture — *height
= where accessibility stops, depth = where the valuation stops being constant* — is exactly right. It
fails only when the tags differ from one another, and then the second cut point is supplied not by
the valuation but by a rival tag.
</details>

---

## 5. The height gap: a weaker tag caps a stronger one

Rigidity is qualitative. There is a second, quantitative obstruction, delivered by one explicit
formula — the **gap probe**
$$G^{s}_{i,j} \;=\; \Box_i^{\,s}\bigl(\Box_j\bot \to \Box_i\bot\bigr),$$
of box depth exactly $s+1$, whose content is "if the weaker tag is inconsistent, so am I", boxed
$s$ times. Its truth pattern is completely explicit: it holds at a world $m$ iff $m$ is above the
reach of tag $i$ or within $s$ steps of the reach of tag $j$. Slide $s$ upward in the widget and
watch the frontier move one world per unit of box depth.

{{interactive_demo:1}}

The consequences, for a tag $i$ strictly higher than a tag $j$:

* **height-gap inequality:** $\rho_i \le H_i - H_j$;
* **low-tag collapse:** $\rho_j \le 1$;
* hence any two tags of reflection depth $\ge 2$ have exactly the same height.

{{visualization:2}}

---

## 6. The bounds are exactly right

Negative results deserve matching constructions. Take a two-valued height vector: some tags high, at
height $N$, some low, at height $L$ with $1 \le L < N$, under the information-free valuation in which
no atom is ever true. Then the reflection depths are **exactly** $N - L$ at the high tags and exactly
$1$ at the low ones — the maxima the two inequalities permit. So on two-valued height vectors the
depth vector is not a free parameter at all; it is a computable function of the height vector.

{{visualization:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>The horizon lemma: why the high tags reach exactly the gap</b></summary>

Under the flat valuation, two worlds $m$ and $n$ satisfy the same formulas of box depth $\le k$ as
soon as $\min(m, L+k) = \min(n, L+k)$. The reason is a back-and-forth game: the low tags freeze the
visible horizon at $L$, and each box in a formula moves the horizon down by one, so a formula of box
depth $k$ can count no further than $L+k$. In particular the top world $N$ stays indistinguishable
from $N-1$ — which the high tag *does* see — until depth $N-L$, exactly where the gap probe strikes.
</details>

{{algorithm:0}}

## 7. Decoupling: making the conjecture true outside the class

If nested fields of view are the culprit, widen the windows. Give tag $i$ both a top cut $H_i$ and a
bottom cut $b_i$: it inspects $n < m$ only when $m \le H_i$ and $n \ge b_i$. Such relations are still
transitive, so still legitimate; their fields of view are intervals $[b_i, \min(N,H_i))$.

Fix $h \ge 2$, take the chain $0,\dots,h+1$, let tag $0$ look down from the worlds $m \le h$ and see

## 9. What to take away

* A provable box sees only the **image** of its tag's accessibility relation; everything else follows.
* **Rigidity is nesting, freedom is incomparability.** Tags that differ only in how far *up* they
